title: Lines, Angles, and Triangles, Part 2: Medium and Hard Problems

beats.say: In part one, we used the angle sum of a triangle, and the angle pairs that parallel lines create.
In this video, we use an isosceles triangle, and then similar triangles, where corresponding sides are proportional.
Medium example. An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of forty degrees, between its two equal sides. What's the measure of each base angle?
In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite the equal sides are equal. The two base angles are opposite the two equal sides, so they match each other.

card.text: The two base angles are equal

beats.say: The three angles add to one hundred eighty. So the two base angles together make one hundred eighty minus forty. We then split that equally.
One hundred eighty minus forty is one hundred forty. This is the total of the two base angles.
One hundred forty divided by two is seventy. So each base angle measures seventy degrees.
Hard example. In triangle P Q R, point S is on P Q and point T is on P R, with S T parallel to Q R. If P S is six, S Q is four, and S T is nine, what's Q R?

scenes.title: Hard: why the triangles are similar

beats.say: Because S T is parallel to Q R, corresponding angles match. Both triangles share the angle at P, so triangle P S T is similar to triangle P Q R.
Now match the sides from the shared vertex P. The side P S corresponds to the whole side P Q, not to the piece S Q. And P Q is six plus four, which is ten.
Let x be Q R. The small triangle's side S T corresponds to the large triangle's side Q R, and P S corresponds to P Q. So nine over x equals six over ten.
Cross-multiply, which means multiplying diagonally. Six times x equals nine times ten, which is ninety.
Divide both sides by six. Ninety divided by six is fifteen. So Q R is fifteen.

Check with the scale factor. The large triangle's side P Q is ten, and the small triangle's side P S is six, so the scale factor is ten over six, which is five thirds. Nine times five thirds is fifteen.
To recap. In an isosceles triangle, subtract the known angle from one hundred eighty, and split the rest between the two equal angles.
A segment parallel to one side cuts off a similar triangle. Match the sides from the shared vertex, using the whole side, not the piece.
beats.item: Similar triangles: use the whole side
